narrative: A hawkish split at the Fed and uncertainty over terminal rates dominate the weekend tape, setting up a USD recovery attempt against its G10 peers at the Sydney open. EUR/USD closed Friday at 1.1527, facing downside risk as the +146bp OIS carry advantage favors the USD despite firm Eurozone inflation. US labor market data takes center stage this week; a strong print would likely extend the USD bid and pressure GBP/USD from its Friday close of 1.3482, where retail sentiment is already 66% short. USD/JPY closed Friday at 157.40, with a strong -2.53 risk reversal skew suggesting any hawkish Fed repricing would sharply challenge recent JPY outperformance ahead of the September FOMC.
